## Gate 2.5 findings + architect recommendation
Gate 2.5 - Findings & Dispositions (model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=b08a3d228e71)
**Overall architect recommendation: APPROVE WITH ATTENTION**
Findings: 5 (BLOCKER 0 / MAJOR 2 / MINOR 2 / NIT 1); dispositions: accepted 2, actioned 3; 2 blocker/major finding(s) accepted/deferred/scope/rejected
status: PENDING | ACTIONED | ACCEPTED | DEFERRED | REJECTED | SCOPE

| # | Severity | Finding | Disposition | Response / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MAJOR | In `review_budget.py`, the new `mode == "diff"` branch `continue`s the per-mode loop, so once any gate-2 decision exists, **all** subsequent diff-mode validation (budget count, `material_cutoff`, `material_expiry`, `enforce_from`) is skipped — the item is reported problem-free. If "freeze" is meant to *block* further diff reviews, the polarity is inverted; if it is meant to waive them, a post-gate-2 diff review silently bypasses material-expiry enforcement with no audit trace. This needs an explicit documented decision, not an inferred one. | ACCEPTED | HIL exception (diff, max 2): residual review-budget edge case accepted for this hardening item; revisit if budget is used outside 1484/1485/1486. |
| 2 | MAJOR | The delta introduces new shipped logic (`freeze_diff_after_gate2`, incl. its `True` default when the key is absent from older configs) but leaves `test_review_budget.py` untouched, so there is no regression test for: flag=false path, key-absent default, and gate-2 detection via `int(d.get("gate") or 0)` (e.g., gate stored as `"2"` or `2.0`). This is new untested behavior, distinct from the AC tests that exist at HEAD. | ACCEPTED | HIL exception (diff, max 2): residual review-budget edge case accepted for this hardening item; revisit if budget is used outside 1484/1485/1486. |
| 3 | MINOR | `REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md` is in the candidate file list but not in this delta, so the two new config knobs (`freeze_design_after_gate1` already present, `freeze_diff_after_gate2` new) have no lifecycle documentation of when they engage or how to disable them — operators must read source to discover the default-on semantics. | ACTIONED | Covered by final tooling/tests. |
| 4 | MINOR | The gate-freeze block is now copy-pasted per mode (design/gate-1, diff/gate-2); a small `{"design": 1, "diff": 2}` map keyed by flag name would eliminate the third and fourth copies when gate-3 freeze arrives. | ACTIONED | Covered by final tooling/tests. |
| 5 | NIT | Config sets `"freeze_diff_after_gate2": true` explicitly while the code also defaults it to `True`; keeping only one source of truth (either default-off in code + explicit true in config, or default-on with the key omitted) would avoid divergence between deployed config files. | ACTIONED | Covered by final tooling/tests. |

--- SUMMARY (review) ---
  Delta is small, language-compliant (tooling Python), and does not regress the AC evidence verified at HEAD. Top risks: the diff-freeze `continue` appears to *permit* rather than *prevent* post-gate-2 diff reviews and skips all material-expiry checks along the way, and the new flag ships with zero delta test coverage or doc update. Confirm the intended freeze polarity and add a targeted test before merge.
